source_text: ἄρτους. Δύο δεκάτων ἔσται ὁ ἄρτος ὁ εἶς, καὶ ἐπιθήσετε αὐτοὺς δύο θέματα, ἓξ ἄρτους τὸ ἓν θέμα ἐπὶ τὴν τράπεζαν τὴν καθαρὰν ἔναντι Κυρίου, καὶ ἐπιθήσετε ἐπὶ τὸ θέμα λίβανον καθαρὸν καὶ ἅλα, καὶ ἔσονται εἰς ἄρτους εἰς ἀνάμνησιν προκείμενα τῷ Κυρίῳ. Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων προθήσετε ἔναντι Κυρίου διαπαντὸς ἐνώπιον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, διαθήκην αἰώνιον· καὶ ἔσται Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φάγονται αὐτὰ ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ· ἔστι γὰρ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων. Τοῦτο αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῶν θυσιαζομένων τῷ Κυρίῳ, νόμιμον αἰώνιον.» Καθαρὸν οὖν τὸ ἔλαιον, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἐλάϊνον, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἐξ ἐλαιῶν, οὐκ ἐξ ἑτεροειδῶν σπερμάτων καὶ γεωδεστέρων, ἐξ ὧν ἔλαιον μὲν ἐθλίβετο, νόθον δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ οἱονεὶ κεκαπηλευμένον· ἀεὶ γάρ ἐστι καθαρὸν καὶ γνήσιον ἀληθῶς ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις τὸ φῶς, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὸ διὰ Χριστοῦ, Πνεύματι, κἂν εἰ διὰ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων διακονοῖτο φωνῆς, πρὸς οὓς ἔφη Χριστός· «Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου.» Καὶ θαυμαστὸν οὐδέν· οὓς γὰρ ἀδελφοὺς ὠνόμασε, καὶ μετόχους ἑαυτοῦ κατεστήσατο, τούτοις ἂν εἰκότως καὶ τῶν ἰδίων ἀξιωμάτων ἐπιμερίζοι τὴν δόξαν. Καίεται δὴ οὖν ὁ λύχνος καὶ ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ, καὶ διττὸν ἂν ἔχοι τὸ χρῆμα τὸν νοῦν· ἐν μὲν γὰρ τῇ ἐσωτέρᾳ σκηνῇ λύχνοι φαίνουσιν ἑπτὰ, ἐξαπτόμενοι τὸ πρωΐ, καὶ πλούσιον τοῖς εἰστρέχουσιν ἐνιέντες τὸ φῶς. Καὶ ἦν ἡ λυχνία Χριστὸς, ὡς ἐν τύπῳ πάλιν τοὺς εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰστρέχειν ἐθέλοντας πολλῷ καὶ ἀμφιλαφεῖ καταυγάζων φωτί· «Προσέλθετε γὰρ, φησὶ, πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ φωτίσθητε.» Καὶ μὴν καὶ τὸ ἀνακαίεσθαι τὸ πρωῒ τοὺς λύχνους κατασημήνειεν ἂν τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως τὸν καιρόν. Διηύγασε γὰρ, οἷά τις ἡμέρα, καὶ φῶς ἀνέλαμψε νοητὸν, τῆς ἀρχαίας ἡμῶν ἀμαθίας ἐλαύνων τὸν σκότον, καὶ ὡς ἐν τάξει νυκτὸς, τὴν ἐπισκήψασαν ταῖς ἁπάντων καρδίαις κατασκεδαννύων ἀχλύν. Οὕτω γὰρ ἡμῖν τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιδημίας τὸν καιρὸν καὶ ὁ προφήτης παρεκάλει λέγων· «Τὸ πρωῒ εἰσακούσῃ τῆς φωνῆς μου, τὸ πρωῒ παραστήσομαί σοι, καὶ ἐπόψομαι.» Πότε γὰρ ἂν δεκταὶ γεγόνασιν αἱ ἁπάντων εὐχαὶ, καὶ οἱ πάλαι πλανώμενοι παρέστημεν οἱονεὶ τῷ Θεῷ, δι' οἰκειότητος, δηλονότι τῆς πνευματικῆς, καὶ ὑπακοῆς καὶ πίστεως, εἰ μὴ τὸ φῶς ἡμῖν ἐπέλαμψε τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι, Χριστός; Οὐκοῦν ἐν μὲν τῇ ἐσωτέρᾳ σκηνῇ πλούσιόν τε καὶ λεπτὸν τῶν ἑπτὰ λύχνων τὸ φῶς, ἐν δὲ τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ λύχνος ἦν ὁ φαίνων, ἐμφαίνων τε, οἶμαι, μὴ δίχα τοῦ θείου φωτὸς, μηδὲ αὐτοὺς εἶναι τοὺς ἐν νόμῳ παιδαγωγουμένους καταδηλοῦντος τοῦ πράγματος. Ἐκάλει γὰρ ἐκ πολυθεΐας εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ φύσει τε καὶ ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ καὶ ὁ διὰ Μωσέως νόμος, καὶ ἀφίστα μὲν τοὺς ἀρχαιοτέρους τοῦ λατρεύειν ἔτι τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν Κτίσαντα, προσκεῖσθαι δὲ δεῖν ἀνέπειθε τῷ πάντων Δημιουργῷ· φωτὸς δὲ οὐ δίχα τοῦ νοητοῦ ταυτὶ ταῖς τῶν παιδαγωγουμένων κατωρθοῦτο ψυχαῖς. Οὐκοῦν, ἐρῶ γὰρ εἰσαῦθις, πλούσιος μὲν καὶ πολὺς τοῖς εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων ὁ παρὰ Χριστοῦ φωτισμὸς, μείων δὲ τοῖς ἐν νόμῳ· καὶ ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος
pass_a_gloss: (Cyril, quotation of Leviticus 24 continuing) '…loaves (ἄρτους). Of two tenths (δύο δεκάτων) will be the one loaf, and you will set them two settings/rows (θέματα), six loaves the one row, upon the pure table before the Lord, and you will put upon the row pure frankincense (λίβανος) and salt (ἅλα), and they will be for the loaves unto remembrance (ἀνάμνησις), set before (προκείμενα) the Lord. On the day of the Sabbaths you will set forth before the Lord continually before the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant (διαθήκη αἰώνιος); and it will be Aaron's and his sons', and they will eat them in a holy place; for it is Holy of holies (Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων). This is his from the things sacrificed to the Lord, everlasting ordinance.' Pure (καθαρόν) then the oil, and indeed also of olive (ἐλάϊνον), that is, from olives, not from seeds of other kind (ἑτεροειδῶν σπερμάτων) and more earthy (γεωδεστέρων), from which oil was pressed (ἐθλίβετο), yet spurious (νόθον) and as it were adulterated (κεκαπηλευμένον); for always pure and truly genuine (γνήσιον) is the light in the churches (ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις), clearly the one through Christ, by the Spirit (Πνεύματι), even if it should be ministered (διακονοῖτο) through the voice of the saints, to whom Christ said: 'You are the light of the world.' And nothing wonderful; for whom he named brothers (ἀδελφούς) and established as partakers (μετόχους) of himself, to these he would fittingly also apportion (ἐπιμερίζοι) the glory of his own dignities (ἀξιωμάτων). So the lamp burns also in the first tent, and the thing would have a double sense (διττὸν νοῦν): for in the inner tent (ἐσωτέρᾳ σκηνῇ) seven lamps shine, kindled (ἐξαπτόμενοι) in the morning, and putting rich light into those running in. And the lampstand (λυχνία) was Christ, as in a type (τύπος) again, illuminating with much and abundant (ἀμφιλαφεῖ) light those wishing to run into the Holy of holies: 'For come to him,' he says, 'and be enlightened (φωτίσθητε).' And indeed the lighting-up (ἀνακαίεσθαι) of the lamps in the morning would signify the time of the becoming-man (ἐνανθρώπησις). For it dawned through (διηύγασε) like a day, and an intelligible light (φῶς νοητόν) shone up, driving the darkness of our ancient ignorance (ἀμαθία), and, as in the order/place of night, scattering the mist (ἀχλύς) that had fallen upon the hearts of all. For thus the prophet too was calling for (παρεκάλει) for us the time of the Savior's sojourn (ἐπιδημία), saying: 'In the morning you will hear my voice, in the morning I will stand before you, and I will look/watch (ἐπόψομαι).' For when would the prayers of all have become acceptable (δεκταί), and we who once wandered (πλανώμενοι) have stood beside (παρέστημεν) God as it were, through kinship/belonging (οἰκειότης), clearly the spiritual one, and obedience (ὑπακοή) and faith (πίστις), unless the light from heaven, that is Christ, had shone upon us? Therefore in the inner tent rich and fine (λεπτόν) the light of the seven lamps, but in the first tent a lamp was the one shining, showing (ἐμφαίνων), I think, that not even those being tutored in law (ἐν νόμῳ παιδαγωγουμένους) themselves were without the divine light, the thing making it plain. For the law through Moses also called from polytheism (πολυθεΐα) unto knowledge (ἐπίγνωσις) of the one who is God by nature and truly, and removed the more ancient from still serving/worshipping (λατρεύειν) the creation (κτίσις) beside/rather than (παρά) the one who created (Κτίσαντα), and persuaded that one must cleave (προσκεῖσθαι) to the Creator (Δημιουργός) of all; and not without the intelligible light were these things accomplished (κατωρθοῦτο) in the souls of those being tutored. Therefore — for I will say again — rich and much is the illumination (φωτισμός) from Christ for those [entering] into the Holy of holies, but lesser (μείων) for those in law; and the word is true [continues in §16 with γάρ].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …loaves. Each loaf shall be of two tenths, and you shall set them in two rows, six loaves to a row, on the pure table before the Lord. And you shall put pure frankincense and salt on the row, and these shall go with the loaves as a memorial, set before the Lord. On the Sabbath day you shall set them out before the Lord continually, in the presence of the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant. And they shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat them in a holy place, for it is a most holy thing. This is his share from the offerings sacrificed to the Lord, a perpetual ordinance’ (Leviticus 24:5–9).

The oil, then, is pure, and it is olive oil besides: that is, it comes from olives, not from other, more earthy kinds of seed, which did yield pressed oil, but oil that was spurious and, so to speak, adulterated. For the light in the churches is always pure and truly genuine: the light, clearly, that comes through Christ, by the Spirit, even if it is ministered through the voice of the saints, to whom Christ said: ‘You are the light of the world’ (Matthew 5:14). And this is no wonder. For with those whom he called his brothers (Hebrews 2:11) and made partakers of himself (Hebrews 3:14), he would fittingly share the glory of his own honors as well.

So the lamp burns in the first tent as well, and the matter would have a twofold sense. In the inner tent seven lamps shine (Exodus 25:37); they are kindled in the morning, and they pour a rich light upon those who hurry in. And the lampstand was Christ, again as in a type, flooding with abundant and generous light those who wish to hurry into the Holy of Holies. For, it says, ‘Come to him and be enlightened’ (Psalm 34:5). Moreover, the lighting of the lamps in the morning would signify the time when he became man. For something like a day dawned, and a light perceived by the mind shone out, driving away the darkness of our ancient ignorance and scattering the mist that had fallen like night upon the hearts of all. So too the prophet called for the time of the Savior’s coming among us, when he said: ‘In the morning you will hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before you, and I will keep watch’ (Psalm 5:3). For when would the prayers of all have become acceptable, and when would we who once wandered have stood, as it were, before God, through kinship with him (the spiritual kind, of course) and through obedience and faith, if the light from heaven, that is, Christ, had not shone upon us?

So in the inner tent the light of the seven lamps is rich and clear, but in the first tent it was a single lamp that gave light; and it showed, I think, that not even those being schooled under the law were without the divine light, as the thing itself makes plain. For the law given through Moses also called people out of the worship of many gods to the knowledge of him who is God by nature and in truth. It drew the people of old away from still serving the creation rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25), and persuaded them that they must hold fast to the Maker of all. And these things were not achieved in the souls of those under its schooling without the light perceived by the mind. So, to say it once more, the illumination that comes from Christ is rich and plentiful for those who enter the Holy of Holies, but less for those under the law; and the statement is true.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation (Leviticus 24:5, 'twelve | loaves'), so the first paragraph begins with an ellipsis under Cyril's label; the whole section is one Cyril speech, split into natural paragraphs. 'And salt' in Leviticus 24:7 is an LXX plus (not in the Hebrew). Leviticus 24:9 Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων rendered 'a most holy thing' in the quotation, but 'the Holy of Holies' where Cyril uses the same phrase for the inner sanctuary. 'Olive oil besides' renders καὶ μὴν καὶ ἐλάϊνον: Cyril supplies the LXX ἐλάινον of Leviticus 24:2 that his quotation in §14 left out. κεκαπηλευμένον ('adulterated', literally 'hawked like a huckster's wine') may echo 2 Corinthians 2:17; uncited. 'Named his brothers … made partakers of himself' cited to Hebrews 2:11 and Hebrews 3:14 as clear Hebrews echoes (Cyril has just quoted Hebrews 7:26); not quotations. Seven lamps: Exodus 25:37 (also Numbers 8:2); Cyril places the seven-lamp lampstand in the 'inner tent' and the single lamp of Leviticus 24:2–4 in the 'first tent'; the English keeps his arrangement without correcting it. The lamps being 'kindled in the morning' is left uncited (compare Exodus 30:7–8, where Aaron tends the lamps morning and evening). Psalm 34:5 = LXX Psalm 33:6 ('Come to him and be enlightened'). Psalm 5:3 = LXX Psalm 5:4; ἐπόψομαι is first person with no object ('and I will look / keep watch'), rendered 'I will keep watch'. ἐνανθρώπησις rendered 'the time when he became man' (literally 'the becoming-man', i.e. the Incarnation). παρεκάλει ('called for, summoned') is kept as 'called for'; a scribal slip for παρεδήλου ('indicated') is possible but not assumed. 'The law given through Moses' may echo John 1:17; uncited as a common phrase. παιδαγωγούμενοι ('being schooled') recalls Galatians 3:24 (the law as tutor); uncited. Διηύγασε ('it dawned') may echo 2 Peter 1:19; uncited.
